methodology: Formal validity and learning quality are separate. Flags are deterministic review signals; abstract meanings and variant forms are not automatically bad, while generic filler is a rewrite signal.

generic_filler.description: Template prose names the pieces but supplies no character-specific causal image.

tautological_self_form.description: A self-form card restates its gloss without describing a memorable visible feature.

duplicated_component_meaning.description: Two components have the same or near-identical learner-facing gloss.

opaque_component_gloss.description: A component gloss is metadata or a placeholder rather than a visual memory object.

abstract_final_meaning.description: The final meaning is abstract, so the causal image needs especially careful review.

unhelpful_final_gloss.description: The final English gloss is grammatical or dictionary-derived but poor for a first-time learner.

variant_form_needs_review.description: An aliased simplified, traditional, Japanese, or compatibility form may need its own visual story.

historical_decomposition_dominates.description: Mnemonic prose foregrounds historical components that are not the main visible decomposition.

weak_causal_link.description: The sentence is grammatical but does not make the final meaning follow from the components.

learner_facing_weirdness.description: Awkward articles, filler adjectives, or unnatural wording interfere with recall.

component_name_only.description: A required component is mentioned but has no essential visible or honestly phonetic job.

invented_load_bearing_prop.description: An added prop, agent, or premise supplies the target meaning instead of the components.

target_leakage.description: The target is introduced as the actor, setting, or label and then merely restated.

ungrammatical_embedding.description: Exact required pairs were inserted into English that is not grammatical on rereading.

corrupt_gloss.description: The supplied target gloss is malformed or a metadata placeholder and needs source repair.

pronunciation_pun.description: The semantic mnemonic relies on a sound-alike, rhyme, pitch, or animal-noise pun.
